sections.html:
New Iberia is the largest city and the parish seat of Iberia Parish, about 21 miles southeast of Lafayette in the Acadiana region, and it belongs to the Lafayette metro area. The 2020 census counted 28,555 residents. The city covers 10.6 square miles, all of it land, at roughly 16 to 20 feet above mean sea level, on Bayou Teche.

Sugar cane is a principal crop for local farmers, and Avery Island, home of Tabasco sauce, sits nearby. U.S. 90, the main four-lane highway, is designated as future Interstate 49. Scheduled passenger flights leave from Lafayette Regional Airport, so easy access to U.S. 90 is a fair point to raise when you describe a house.

New Iberia has a subtropical climate with above-average rainfall. The annual average high is 79.1 degrees and the average low is 59.4 degrees. Hurricane Ike flooded parts of the city in September 2008.

Flood history, roof age and drainage are the three things a buyer's insurer will likely ask about. Pull any past claims and repair receipts before a sale, because gaps in paperwork slow a conventional closing more than the repairs themselves. Check the flood zone for your specific address before listing.

The city's Compliance and Right-of-Way Office enforces ordinances, especially condemnation of houses, grass, abandoned vehicles and junk.

  • Complaints about abandoned houses, high grass, junk and junk vehicles go to (337) 369-2354.
  • The office is at 457 E. Main Street, Suite 412, New Iberia, LA 70560.
  • Complaints can also be filed through an online code portal linked from the city page.
  • Outside the city limits, Iberia Parish Government has a Report a Nuisance page, with permits staff at 715-A Weldon Street and the phone number 337-369-4438.

A vacant house is an easy target for a complaint about grass or condition. Ask the office whether anything is open on your address before you accept a sale date. State law also created the New Iberia Redevelopment Authority to address blighted and distressed areas (R.S. 33:4720.181).

sections.h2: How does the Iberia Parish Assessor set value and tax?
sections.html:
The assessor appraises roughly 68,000 parcels. Assessed value is a percentage of fair market value: land and residential improvements at 10 percent, commercial improvements and commercial personal property at 15 percent, and public service property at 25 percent. A home with a signed homestead exemption can deduct up to $7,500 from assessed value for parish purposes. Parish rates and city rates differ, and the homestead deduction applies to the parish side.

For questions about an assessment or a mailing address, call the assessor at (337) 369-4415.

sections.h2: When are New Iberia property taxes due, and who collects them?
sections.html:
The Iberia Parish Sheriff is the tax collector for parish taxes. Notices are mailed in November and are due by December 31 of that year. The city mails and collects its own taxes at rates the city sets, and several other bodies add millages, including the school board, parish council and fire or recreation districts, depending on where the property is.

sections.h2: Recording fees at the Iberia Parish Clerk of Court
sections.html:
The Iberia Parish Clerk of Court records conveyances and mortgages at 300 Iberia Street, Suite 100, New Iberia. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, and the phone is 337-365-7282.

  • 1 to 5 pages: $110.
  • 6 to 25 pages: $210.
  • 26 to 50 pages: $310.
  • 51 or more pages: $310 plus $5 per extra page.
  • Cancellation or partial release: $60. Mortgage certificate for one name and one property: $20.

These fees already include a $5 payment to Iberia Parish Government and a $5 statewide portal fee. Fees are assessed separately for each recording book. Clerk staff can point you to records but are not abstractors or attorneys, so title research takes a professional.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in New Iberia
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, a notary or attorney orders a title search and your lender supplies a payoff. Have your deed, latest tax bill, flood and roof records ready, and, for a rental, the lease. A financed buyer adds an appraisal and inspection. A cash buyer can close once the title is clear. Taxes, your mortgage balance and recording fees come out of your proceeds at the signing. Ask for the settlement statement early so you can question any charge.

Buyers with children usually ask which school campus a house feeds, and the Iberia Parish School System can give you its own boundary information to pass along.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or vacant house
sections.html:
Heirs often hold a New Iberia house for months before deciding what to do. During that time grass grows, a complaint can be filed, and taxes keep coming due. Start by finding out who has the authority to sign, which usually means a notary or attorney helping with the succession. Then call the compliance office about any open case, and ask the sheriff and the assessor whether taxes are current and where notices are being mailed.

Cleaning the lot and removing junk before you show the house often costs little and keeps a minor complaint from becoming a lien that has to be paid at closing.

sections.h2: What to gather before you talk to buyers
sections.html: Collect the deed, the most recent tax bill, your mortgage servicer's contact details, insurance claim records, repair receipts and any flood or elevation paperwork. For a rental, add the lease and its end date. Having these ready lets a notary start the title work immediately and lets a cash buyer make a firm offer without a long round of questions. Keep copies of everything you sign, including the settlement statement and the recorded act of sale.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a New Iberia house?
sections.html:
A cash sale can fit an inherited house with a code complaint, a property with flood or roof damage, or a rental the owner wants out of. The buyer takes the property as it is, so lender appraisal conditions drop out. Liens, taxes and succession questions still have to be resolved with a notary or attorney.

Compare any cash price with what a listing would leave after repairs and carrying costs, and ask every buyer to put the closing date and conditions in writing. You skip weeks of showings with cash, but expect a lower price than a repaired listing might reach.

faqs.q: Who do I call about an abandoned house in New Iberia?
faqs.a: The city's Compliance and Right-of-Way Office takes complaints at (337) 369-2354. It enforces rules on abandoned houses, high grass, junk and junk vehicles.

faqs.q: When are Iberia Parish property taxes due?
faqs.a: Notices are mailed in November and are due by December 31. The Iberia Parish Sheriff collects the parish taxes, and the city collects its own.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead deduction in Iberia Parish?
faqs.a: A homeowner who has signed for the homestead exemption can deduct up to $7,500 of assessed value. Contact the assessor at (337) 369-4415 to check eligibility.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Iberia Parish?
faqs.a: A document of 1 to 5 pages costs $110, 6 to 25 pages costs $210, and 26 to 50 pages costs $310.

faqs.q: Can I sell a New Iberia house with an open code complaint?
faqs.a: Yes, but ask the compliance office what is open and whether fines or a condemnation process apply. Cash buyers can take the house as it stands.
